reviews.text: Competent but not quite what it thinks it is. The mystery proper -- who killed Calloway and why -- is solved with workmanlike efficiency, and the clue work with the blotter palimpsest is rather good. But the story seems more interested in the detective's moral limitations than in the puzzle itself, and I confess I find that gambit somewhat overplayed in contemporary crime fiction. We are meant to understand that Nora is 'right about everything except what her solution means,' and the story is quite insistent about this, turning every observation she makes into an occasion for ironic commentary. The four suspects are well-differentiated in interview, I'll grant that -- Garrick anticipating her questions, Leroy's shift from management to charm. The prose is controlled and the setting vivid. But the ending simply stops. Rain, coffee, an empty street. One expects more from a story that has been so carefully constructed.
